📋 Features

Everything a register does. Plus everything it can't.

Built around how Indian classrooms actually run — roll numbers, WhatsApp groups, and a Principal who wants the full picture without chasing teachers for it.

✅

Mark attendance in one tap per student

Teachers open a class, tap Present or Absent against each roll number, and save — no separate register, no end-of-month re-entry into Excel.

💬

WhatsApp absence alerts

Notify a parent the moment a student is marked absent, straight from the attendance screen.

📄

PDF reports, generated instantly

Day-wise attendance, shortage lists, and percentage summaries — exported as a clean PDF for any date range.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑

Role-based dashboards

Principals see the whole school, teachers see their classes, and students see only their own record — nothing more, nothing less.

📥

Clerk portal for bulk uploads

Share a one-time code with your office clerk — they upload the full student list from Excel in one go, no manual typing.

🌱

Attendance streaks & class leaderboards for students

A daily streak garden and a monthly class ranking give students their own reason to show up — attendance stops being something that only happens to them.

📅

Subject-wise calendar

Every student can see a full month at a glance, colour-coded present and absent, subject by subject.

About Attendance App
🏫Made for All country schools & colleges
🧾Terms, privacy policy & a named Grievance Officer under the IT Act, 2000

Why another attendance app?

Most attendance software is built for a generic classroom that doesn't quite match how Indian schools and colleges actually work — roll numbers that matter more than names, a clerk who handles the paperwork, and a Principal who's ultimately accountable for every number in the register.

Attendance App was built around that reality instead of around it. A teacher marks attendance the way they already think about a class — roll number by roll number. A clerk can onboard an entire school's student list from an Excel sheet they already have. And a student, for the first time, gets to see their own attendance without asking anyone for it.

It's a small, focused app doing one job well — not a bloated "school ERP" trying to do everything at once.
